vsProforma.basis: Fastest direct proforma on the pair with an in-window departure: Evergreen NUE2, COSCO SHIPPING ORCHID 035E, Ningbo 13 Sep, 25d. AA9 runs 38d Ningbo to New York, 13 days slower, and 45d Ningbo to Savannah. src.wanhai: SkdBySvcCsv.jsp srv_code AA9 bound E, pulled 2026-09-03 in the single permitted burst alongside AA6 AA7 AA8 AA10 AA11. Header reads 'Asia America Service IX LONG TERM SCHEDULE', generation date 2026/09/03. The whole service file contains exactly one vessel, WAN HAI 712, on two voyage lines: E001 with Ningbo and Qingdao calls and no US calls at all, and E002 with the full US rotation. A named service with a single ship and no second sailing anywhere in the file is an ad-hoc voyage wearing a service code, not a proforma loop.
src.note: Rotation and all dates are byte-identical to the 2026-09-02 reading. AA6, AA8, AA10 and AA11 all returned empty 85-byte files, so no sister voyages exist. AA7 returned a full multi-vessel schedule and is registry-known (Wan Hai / Hapag VSA), correctly not flagged.

MSC is back after one run blocked. The fix: POST /api/feature/tools/SearchSailingRoutes accepts dataSourceId as an empty string, so no captured token is needed. Body is {FromDate, fromPortId, toPortId, language, dataSourceId} as JSON with X-Requested-With XMLHttpRequest. Port ids come from GET /api/feature/tools/GetAllAvailableCountriesAndPorts (Yantian 2, Savannah 70, New York 79, Houston 86, Busan 274, Ningbo 441, Shanghai 444). Seven lanes returned clean, every MaritimeServiceName registry-known: AMERICA, EMERALD, EMPIRE, LONE STAR EXPRESS. No candidates.

Not covered. No DataDome 403 this run - the block is different. The routing-finder page loads, but /api/PortsWithInlands/GetAllPlaces returns an empty array for every parameter name tried (term, query, search, keyword, name, q, prefix), the Kendo autocomplete on #AutoCompletePOL never populates its dataSource when driven programmatically, and after two attempts the renderer wedged: screenshot and script injection both timed out at 45s and did not recover. The POST target is /ebusiness/schedules/routing-finder with fields ActualPOLDescription, ActualPODDescription, polType, podType, IsDeparture, SearchDate, searchRange - what is missing is the place-code format. Worth a targeted fix next run.

Not covered. The point-to-point form is inside shadow DOM behind an undismissed cookie consent banner. The From field accepted Yantian through a real click and keystrokes, but selecting the destination re-rendered the page and moved every coordinate, and there is no Search button in the accessibility tree until both fields are set. Accepting a consent banner needs explicit permission and is out of scope for an unattended run, and the routing-unified replay needs headers captured from a completed UI search. api.maersk.com/synergy/reference-data/locations returns ApplicationNotFound, so there is no unauthenticated place lookup. Mitigating factor: Maersk sails the Gemini network, which Hapag-Lloyd's public API already covers end to end, so a Gemini extra loader would surface as an unknown serviceCode on the Hapag side.

Not covered, and the failure mode has changed. This is no longer the 'Thanks for Your Patience' throttle - the site has been restructured. ecomm.one-line.com/one-ecom/schedule, /one-ecom/schedule/routing-finder, /one-ecom/schedule/route-finder and /one-ecom/manage-schedule/routing-finder-1 all return ONE's own Not Found page, ecomm.one-line.com/schedule/routing-finder returns a bare Tomcat 404, and www.one-line.com/en/schedules is a Page Not Found. The Route Finder URL in the task file is dead and needs to be rediscovered. ONE also posted a maintenance notice for 6 September. Real consequence: EC1-EC4 (Premier Alliance) has no direct source this run.

Lanes not covered this run: every CMA CGM lane, every Maersk lane and every ONE lane (all 15 origin-destination combinations for each of those three carriers). Evergreen forward visibility is four weeks, not eight, because durationWeek caps at 28 days - a second pass from 2026-10-01 on Yantian to New York returned only 3 rows (SAX 1, AUE 1, CBX 1) and no OGEC, so weeks 41 to 43 of the window are effectively unscanned for Evergreen. Ad-hoc voyages normally surface two to four weeks out, so this is tolerable, but it is not full-window coverage.

OGEC voyage 0022 has not appeared yet. Voyages 0020 (TRITON) and 0021 (EVER LASTING) are consecutive, which makes OGEC a rolling weekly ad-hoc programme rather than a pair of one-offs, so a 0022 is expected. It is absent from both the 03 Sep and the 01 Oct Evergreen passes on Yantian and Shanghai to New York. Check again next run.
